content.jointProblem: Could a script-normalizing, morphology-aware indexing and query pipeline that combines phoneme-based canonicalization with Serbian lemmatization or stemming and cross-script query expansion reduce LinguaBot's measured no-useful-result rate from about 18% to below 5% on real support queries while remaining maintainable as vocabulary changes? The first experiment would test this on LinguaBot's labelled support-query data and current Elasticsearch setup, not assume it transfers from the researcher's existing corpora.

rationale.text: The researcher has a directly relevant method for building an inverted index that handles both Cyrillic and Latin Serbian tokens through phoneme-based canonical forms.

sources.quote: Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji

rationale.text: His work explicitly studies how stemming and lemmatization interact with script normalization, which matches LinguaBot's combined morphological-mismatch and script-confusion problem.

sources.quote: Rezultati pokazuju da redosled operacija (stemovanje pre ili posle normalizacije skripte) utiče na odziv, pri čemu stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije

rationale.text: He has measured cross-script query expansion against a no-expansion baseline, including index-bloat effects relevant to an Elasticsearch deployment.

sources.quote: Strategy 3 achieved the best mean average precision of 0.497, versus 0.431 for no expansion, while reducing index bloat to 6% over the baseline index size.

rationale.text: He has studied latency–accuracy trade-offs for script-normalizing retrieval pipelines, including a cascaded configuration designed to limit neural normalization overhead.

sources.quote: A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms.

rationale.text: He has prior contract-research experience adapting a search module for Serbian court decisions, close to LinguaBot's client-facing document search context.

sources.quote: sarađivao je s jednim novosadskim startapom iz oblasti legaltech-a na prilagođavanju pretražnog modula za srpske sudske odluke

constraints.text: The plan must attack the measured business failure mode: about 18% of real support queries returned no useful result, with more than half of those misses traced to morphological mismatch or script confusion.

sources.quote: about 18% returned no useful result, and our analysis traced more than half of those misses directly to morphological mismatch or script confusion.

constraints.text: The solution must tolerate automatic script mixing and must be updateable when new vocabulary arrives without requiring a full re-index.

sources.quote: can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index

constraints.text: The work must be testable within six months and fit a modest tooling/data budget of about 8,000 EUR.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: Evaluation can use the company's labelled query-response data and its two in-house linguists for annotation or validation.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.

constraints.text: The approach must fit an existing Elasticsearch-based retrieval stack whose current Croatian-oriented stemmer misses Serbian-specific forms.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.

constraints.text: The researcher's stated capacity is one smaller industrial contract or consultancy engagement, not an unlimited scope.

sources.quote: ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman

risks: Transfer gap: much of the researcher's evidence comes from news, legal, benchmark or pilot corpora, not from LinguaBot's bank support queries; the first experiment must test on the company's mixed-script support data. Source: SYN-PUB-04278 reports experiments on a 2000–2008 newspaper corpus.

Maintenance risk: the researcher's own pilot work notes that the module must be updated when a company introduces new terminology in one script, because the initial synonym dictionary is incomplete. Source: SYN-PUB-04285 abstract.

Residual accuracy risk: foreign loanwords, abbreviations and proper nouns are known failure cases for deterministic transliteration, so exception handling must be planned. Source: SYN-PUB-04279 abstract.
Latency risk: a transformer-based normalizer adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile, so production chat/search latency budgets must be checked. Source: SYN-PUB-04287 abstract.
Budget and time risk: the company wants a six-month test with about 8,000 EUR, so data work, integration and evaluation must be tightly scoped. Source: C009-CH1 detail.
Researcher availability is unknown; his notes say he has capacity for one smaller industrial contract, but this does not confirm a six-month joint-project commitment.
questions: Can Stefan Dragić confirm his availability and capacity for a six-month joint project or contract research, and whether industrial PhD supervision is also of interest?
What is the current Elasticsearch index mapping and Serbian analyzer chain, and can script normalization be inserted at both indexing and query time without a full re-index?
What privacy, licensing or client-consent terms apply to the 85,000 labelled query-response pairs and the 12,000-query bank sample?
How exactly is a 'no useful result' defined and measured today, and what baseline and evaluation set will be used to test the below-5% target?
Who will own and maintain the lexicon, exception rules and new product terminology after the six-month project, and how will updates be triggered?
What production latency, throughput and deployment constraints must the retrieval pipeline meet?
